extracted.intended_audience: Public Information Officers (PIOs), PIO trainees, incident information staff, and incident management personnel
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and checklists for Public Information Officers on reporting wildland fire fatalities/entrapments, managing special situations, creating safe environments, and planning/processing demobilization and transition of information staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wildland Fire Fatality and Entrapment — Initial Report (timeliness and routing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Complete this report for fire-related entrapment and/or fatalities. Immediately notify the National Interagency Coordination Center (NICC) Coordinator on Duty (COD) by phone, and then submit this written report to NICC within 24 hours—even if some data are missing. This initial report does not replace agency reporting or investigative responsibilities, policies, or procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include submitter contact (Submitted by, Agency, Phone, E-mail). Use NICC address/phone/fax/COD email provided. Timely reporting is necessary for rapid dissemination of accurate information and to allow safety and equipment specialists to respond. Do not release name(s) until next of kin are notified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fatality/Entrapment Basic Data Fields
rubrics_metrics.description: Report fields to capture essential event data: Date/time of event, Number of personnel involved, Position, Location, Number of injuries, Fatalities, Fire name/location/agency, Type of accident (Aircraft, Vehicle, Natural, Smoke, Medical, Entrapment, Struck by falling object), Where fatality/entrapment occurred (Fire site, In transit, Incident base, Other), Employing agency, Unit name/address, and Contact for further information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide as complete information as possible even if some items are initially missing; use checkboxes where provided to indicate categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entrapment Definition and Reporting Elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Entrapment: 'A situation where personnel are unexpectedly caught in a fire-behavior-related, life-threatening position where escape routes or safety zones are absent, inadequate, or have been compromised.' An entrapment may or may not include deployment of a fire shelter. Engine and dozer burnovers also constitute entrapments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include a brief description of the accident, whether person was with/without shelter, burns/smoke injuries in shelter/while escaping/while fighting fire, whether fire shelter performed satisfactorily or was available but not used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entrapment — Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) and Injury Reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Record use of PPE and injury detail: Fire shelter, Gloves, Protective pants, Boots, Protective shirt, Goggles, Face/neck protection, Hardhat; indicate Yes/No for usage and note burns/smoke injuries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Capture whether shelters were used and how they performed; these data inform safety analyses and equipment evaluations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Activity 8.1: Plan to Manage a Special Situation — Required Plan Components
rubrics_metrics.description: Each group plan should include: a) Statement of the situation, b) Staffing assessment, c) Facilities assessment, d) Action items.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Activity structure: small-group scenario review (approx. 30 minutes), select a spokesperson, develop the plan addressing the four components, and present findings. Facilitators assign scenarios. Instructors moderate and provide information as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incident Action Plan (IAP) Safety Content
rubrics_metrics.description: The Incident Action Plan should include information on the nearest hospital and other emergency services, safety objectives (ICS Form 208 Safety Message/Plan), and medical plans (ICS Form 206 Medical Plan).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Know the location of the Safety Officer and include them in briefings for escorted persons. For biosecurity incidents, include specifics on what to wear, when to remove PPE, and how to dispose of PPE.

rubrics_metrics.name: PIO Responsibility for Media and Escort PPE (Your word is law on safety)
rubrics_metrics.description: If you are with the media, make sure that they know what they should be wearing. IT IS YOUR RESPONSIBILITY TO ENSURE THEIR SAFETY! PPE is required for everyone going to the field/incident.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required PPE examples: Leather boots with 8-inch tops; Leather gloves; Tyvex®; Cotton undergarments; Hard hat; Earplugs and goggles. Brief escorted persons on hazards, PPE, spacing while walking, travel times based on physical condition, the importance of not leaving the group or guide, hazardous road or driving conditions, and warning signs of potential hazard exposure (chemical smells, lightheadedness, tingling, blurred vision, nausea).

rubrics_metrics.name: Communications Protocols for Escorts and Field Movements
rubrics_metrics.description: Communications expectations when escorting or traveling in the incident area.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide radio and frequencies, notify Division Supervisor upon entering and leaving their assigned section, and check in/check out with the Public Information group on destination and expected return.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interface Hazards to Include in Public Messaging
rubrics_metrics.description: Additional hazards—mostly urban—that the Incident Management Team may encounter while managing an incident and that should be part of the PIO message.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include explosives/flammables/pesticides near homes (propane tanks common), toxic gases (manufactured items produce toxic fumes when burned), domestic animals, unpredictable resident behavior (refusal to evacuate, panic, violence), and water contamination (sewer/chemicals) usually from storms and rising water.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vehicle and Road Hazards Checklist
rubrics_metrics.description: Check the Incident Action Plan and security for known road hazards (fire traffic, smoke, dust, sun angle).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remember to: consider vehicle appropriateness for mission (4x4), yield to downhill traffic and traffic with a load, check fluid levels (including gas), always drive with lights on, leave gates as you find them, avoid parking under power lines or fire-weakened/storm-damaged trees/snags, park facing exit direction, watch for tall grass (ignition risk from catalytic converter), keep keys accessible, avoid blocking traffic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aircraft Hazards and Ground Personnel Safety Procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Aircraft hazards include turning rotors, noise, retardant drops, and accidental losses of sling loads. Helicopter and fixed-wing safety protocols define responsibilities for crew and passengers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Helitack crews escort passengers to/from helicopter, load gear, close/open doors, and provide a safety briefing; ensure eye contact with the pilot before approaching; never approach a helicopter from the rear. Fixed-wing pilots open/close doors, provide passenger safety briefings, and load/unload cargo and baggage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Camp Hazards and Personal Self-Care
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider contaminated camps and general welfare of staff.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If camps contaminated: know safe areas (LCES: Lookouts, Communications, Escape Routes, Safety Zones) and keep safety gear nearby. Take care of yourself: be alert to stress and fatigue, take breaks, get rest, drink extra fluids, maintain nutrition. Escorts need hazardous response knowledge to know when it is time to leave.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internally Communicating Safety Hazards — Staffing Decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Base staffing decisions and assignments on several factors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use your knowledge of the job and its hazards; the skills, abilities, desires, and limitations of your workforce; and management objectives and strategies selected to meet those objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Externally Communicating Safety Hazards — Techniques
rubrics_metrics.description: Techniques for communicating safety hazards to external audiences (visuals referenced).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare PIO messages to make the public aware of interface hazards that may potentially affect them; use appropriate messaging techniques for community and media audiences (details in referenced visuals/handouts).

rubrics_metrics.name: PIO Documentation Standards for Demobilization
rubrics_metrics.description: Public Information Officer’s incident documentation and to whom it must be submitted during demobilization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep documentation neat and orderly; box documentation and label with name of incident, date, and incident number; submit to the local Public Affairs Officer at end of the incident (may be turned in to Documentation Unit). Turn over documentation to next Incident Management Team if incident management not finished. Compile materials of interest to Agency Administrator (pictures, newspaper clippings, copies of all products generated by the information office such as news releases, fact sheets).

rubrics_metrics.name: PIO Transition Responsibilities During Demobilization
rubrics_metrics.description: Public Information Officer responsibilities during transition include coordination with command and local PAOs and assessment of future need for information resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Meet with Incident Commander and staff to discuss whether information needs have been met and to get IC critique of Information function. Meet with local Public Affairs Officer to convey observations/recommendations for a post-incident Information Strategic Plan and conduct local agency critique/After Action Review. Assess need for an Information Section (indications of lessening need include reduced incident activity and reduced media/community interest) and consider employee/home unit needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demobilization is Not Mobilization — operational principle
rubrics_metrics.description: Demobilization is not a mirror image of mobilization: mobilization involves many individuals coordinating to get resources to a single point; demobilization is the responsibility of a few people returning resources to departure points or new assignments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan accordingly: demobilization requires tight coordination and oversight by designated units/leaders rather than mass coordination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Components of a Typical Demobilization Plan (PIO inputs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Demobilization Plan should be prepared with input from relevant managers; sample plans and an ICS Form 221 Demobilization Check-Out are referenced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PIO should prepare Demobilization Plan elements and use sample filled-in ICS Form 221 as a template for check-out procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance Evaluations — desired characteristics
rubrics_metrics.description: Appropriate characteristics of performance evaluations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be candid and objective; emphasize results rather than processes; concentrate on situations, not people; emphasize the important issues; be based on objectives and direction provided; be discussed with the individuals; be finalized in face-to-face exchange; be completed before individuals are released from the incident; facilitate a process to deal with substandard performance or conduct; be prepared, documented, and distributed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incident Personnel Performance Rating — process and outputs
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures for evaluating individuals and handling ratings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate individuals as required by agency policy; use ICS Form 225 or equivalent; provide a copy of the rating to the individual; list training and leadership development recommendations if needed or desired; discuss performance with the individual; maintain accuracy and fairness; submit signed form to Documentation Unit.

rubrics_metrics.name: General Demobilization Guidelines (A–J) — release authorization and work/rest
rubrics_metrics.description: General rules governing resource release and travel home/reassignment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A: NO resources will leave the Incident until authorized by the Incident Commander facilitated through the Demobilization Unit. B: All releases and travel will comply with National Work/Rest Guidelines; ensure released personnel arrive home no later than 2200 local time or as authorized by IC; resources have minimum of at least 8 consecutive hours off duty before beginning a shift or demobilization. C: All vehicles leaving incident will have a safety inspection and deficiencies corrected prior to departure; vehicles will be washed to prevent spread of noxious weeds. D: All Party Chiefs, Crew Supervisors, and Strike Team Leaders will be briefed by Demobilization Unit prior to leaving (method of travel, itinerary, manifests with destinations). E: Personnel flying commercial will be given time to shower/dress and require photo I.D. and travel authorization number as needed; Demobilization Unit/Expanded Dispatch will make flight arrangements unless otherwise agreed. F: Notification by posting 'Tentative Releases' in advance; crew supervisors paged when demobilization begins. G: Reassigned resources within Geographic Areas will be released on the original order/request number. H: Contractors/operators of oversize vehicles responsible for obtaining required permits for return trip. I: Actual departure times and ETAs relayed to Expanded Dispatch upon departure. J: Performance Ratings are required for trainees, outstanding performance, deficient performance, and by personal request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demobilization Unit Leader — responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: The Demobilization Unit Leader is responsible for preparing and managing the demobilization process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare the Demobilization Plan with input from center manager/Expanded Dispatch; provide Expanded Dispatch with 'Tentative' releases and confirmation of departing resources (including contract equipment) with departure times and ETDs/ETAs; make advance notification to incident personnel regarding tentative and final releases; ensure all signatures are obtained on ICS Form 221 Demobilization Check-Out; monitor the Demobilization process and make necessary adjustments to maintain an orderly and safe release and accurate/timely release information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incident Commander — demobilization responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: IC responsibilities relative to demobilization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish Incident release priorities in concert with the Geographic Area Coordinator; review and approve the Demobilization Plan and tentative release lists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safety Officer — demobilization responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Safety Officer role in demobilization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify any special safety considerations for the Demobilization Plan and approve tentative surplus resources from a safety perspective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Planning Section Chief — demobilization responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Planning Section Chief role in demobilization oversight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review and approve the Demobilization Plan and tentative release lists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Logistics Section Chief — demobilization responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Logistics responsibilities for release process and personnel/property accounting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure through Facilities Unit that sleeping and work areas are cleaned prior to release; through Supply Unit ensure non-expendable property items are returned or accounted for; through Ground Support ensure adequate ground transportation and vehicle safety inspections prior to leaving (correct deficiencies), prevention of spread of noxious weeds by vehicles; through Communications Unit ensure communications equipment returned/accounted for; through Food Unit ensure adequate meals for those being released and those remaining in camp.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finance Section Chief — demobilization responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Finance responsibilities in demobilization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Completion of all time and equipment reports for released resources; coordination for any ADO payoff(s); contract equipment payments; review and provide excessive shift length justification with IC's signature; approval of tentative surplus (Finance) personnel; review of the Demobilization Plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operations Section Chief — demobilization responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Operations responsibilities in demobilization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review the Demobilization Plan and approve the tentative surplus (Operations) personnel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Liaison Officer — demobilization responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Liaison Officer support for agency-specific demobilization requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide any agency-specific requirements for the Demobilization Plan.

rubrics_metrics.name: Release Priorities (IC-established list)
rubrics_metrics.description: Priority order for releasing resources established by the Incident Commander in concert with Expanded Dispatch/GACC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed priorities: 1) Local Government and OES Engines (Type 1,2,&3) (priorities coordinated with OES Agency Representative); 2) CDF Engines (coord with CDF Agency Rep); 3) CDF Crews; 4) State and Local Government Overhead; 5) Forest Service Engines; 6) Forest Service Type 2 crews; 7) Federal Overhead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Release Procedures — identification, approval, notification, and checkout
rubrics_metrics.description: Stepwise procedures for releasing personnel and resources from the incident.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section Chiefs identify surpluses and submit lists to Demobilization Unit Leader in Planning Section. Demobilization combines lists into 'Tentative Release' lists for Planning Section Chief and Incident Commander review/approval. Demobilization coordinates with Resources Unit to keep resource status board(s) current. All incident-formed strike teams/task forces must be disbanded before IC approval and release. After IC approval, Demobilization notifies Expanded Dispatch, provides minimum 24-hour notice for all resources, and gives Ground Support time to arrange transportation. Demobilization advises Expanded Dispatch of surplus resources specifying those needing air transportation and nearest commercial airport. Expanded Dispatch notifies appropriate GACC/dispatch centers. If reassigned, Expanded Dispatch advises Demobilization and resource released to new assignment; otherwise released back to home unit. When confirmation received, Demobilization instructs personnel to obtain ICS Form 221 and sequentially visit: Communications U.L. (if issued comms), Ground Support U.L. (vehicle inspection), Facilities U.L. (sleeping areas cleaned), Supply U.L. (return non-expendable property), Finance Unit (close out time/get Fire Time Report), Documentation Unit (Unit Logs, performance ratings), and Demobilization U.L. (collect all signatures). Demobilization Unit will be last stop: collect/sign-off ICS Form 221, brief released personnel on travel method/schedule/time frames, release resource from base, advise Expanded Dispatch of ETD/ETA, coordinate with Resources Unit to keep status current, and coordinate with Security for inspection if required by IC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demobilization — Communication of Travel and Contact Information
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide travel-related information and maintain communication channels during demobilization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain Incident Directory with Incident Base phone numbers (Communications, Demobilization, Plans, Supply, Finance, PIO, Ground Support, Expanded Dispatch), radio frequencies (Agency Dispatch, Forest Net, RX/TX). Relay actual departure times and ETAs to Expanded Dispatch upon departure of resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demobilization Plan Review and Approval Signatures
rubrics_metrics.description: Formal review/approval process for demobilization plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Train Incident Demobilization Plan includes required reviews/approvals by Planning Section Chief, Operations Section Chief, Finance Section Chief, Logistics Section Chief, Safety Officer, Liaison Officer, Information Officer and final approval by Incident Commander with date.
